html:
The Xambioá, also called the Karajá do Norte, are an Indigenous people of the lower Araguaia River in the state of Tocantins, Brazil. They are the northern branch of the Karajá, river people who speak a language of the Macro-Jê family, and they fish and farm along the Araguaia.

At the end of the 1800s they numbered about 1,350. Disease, river traffic and settlers cut them to a few dozen in the 20th century, and many now speak Portuguese. In the 1970s the area around the town of Xambioá was the scene of the Araguaia guerrilla war between leftist rebels and the army of the military regime. Neighbours include the Apinajé and Parkatêjê.
